ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Two squares $9 \mathrm{~cm} \times 9 \mathrm{~cm}$ overlap so as to form a rectangle $9 \mathrm{~cm} \times 13 \mathrm{~cm}$ as shown. Find the area of the region in which the two squares overlap.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows two squares of the same height overlapping horizontally, and the outer contour forms a rectangle; the top sides and bottom sides of the two squares are aligned. The middle gray region represents the overlapping part of the two squares, and on the left and right sides there is respectively an unoverlapped white vertical strip region. Reasoning: The side length of each square is 9 cm, so the area of each is 9×9=81 cm². The union after the two squares overlap is the external 9 cm × 13 cm rectangle, with area 9×13=117 cm². By the area inclusion-exclusion formula: union area = sum of the areas of the two squares − overlapping area, so overlapping area = 81+81−117=45 cm².

raw_record.question_text: Two squares $9 \mathrm{~cm} \times 9 \mathrm{~cm}$ overlap so as to form a rectangle $9 \mathrm{~cm} \times 13 \mathrm{~cm}$ as shown. Find the area of the region in which the two squares overlap.

method.method_draft: Use area inclusion-exclusion. From the image, identify that the two 9 cm by 9 cm squares are aligned with the same top and bottom edges, and their union is the outer 9 cm by 13 cm rectangle shown; the gray central rectangle is the overlap. From the text, take each square's area as 9×9 and the total outer rectangle area as 9×13. Apply Area(square 1 ∪ square 2)=Area(square 1)+Area(square 2)−Area(overlap). Thus overlap = 81+81−117 = 45 cm².

method.method_draft: Use horizontal length decomposition. From the image, note that the overlap is a vertical central rectangle spanning the full 9 cm height, because both squares share the same top and bottom boundaries. From the text, each square has horizontal width 9 cm, while the total outside rectangle has horizontal width 13 cm. If the overlap width is x, then placing two 9 cm-wide squares side by side with overlap gives total width 9+9−x=13, so x=5 cm. The overlap area is then height × overlap width = 9×5 = 45 cm².
